description:
Delete the claims-index rebuild, verification and index-write machinery and the recovery step and warnings that used it, now that leases are per-issue records.

## Background

Leases are stored one file per issue under the lease lock, and no lease operation reads the index or the log. What remains of the index model: `rebuild_index_from_log`, `rebuild_index_from_log_at`, `verify_index_consistency`, `write_index_atomic`, `evict_expired` and `load_claims_index` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:872-1360`); `jit recover`'s verify-and-rebuild step (`commands/claim.rs:733-741`), its `index_rebuilt` report field (`main.rs:7246,7259`) and help text (`cli.rs:424`); `StorageWarning::SequenceGap`, `DuplicateLease` and `IndexRebuilt` (`storage/warnings.rs:37-48,98-106,156-175`); the rebuild property tests in `storage/claim_coordinator_proptests.rs` (`prop_index_rebuild_idempotent`, `prop_no_data_loss_in_rebuild`, `prop_staleness_computed_during_rebuild`); and the recovery tests that remove the index (`tests/cli_repo_workflow/claim_integration_tests.rs:750-785`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The listed functions, the three warnings, `RecoveryReport.index_rebuilt` and recovery's verify-and-rebuild step no longer exist; no command rebuilds lease state from the claims log, reads `claims.jsonl` or writes `claims.index.json`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit recover`'s help names exactly its passes: stale-lock cleanup, expired-lease eviction and stale indefinite-lease reclaim.
- [hard] REQ-03: The rebuild property tests and the index-removal recovery tests no longer exist.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Claims-index rebuild machinery is gone
